Relevant phrase in the article :

using federally defined guidelines to include voluntary or involuntary incapacitation due to drugs or alcohol and the threat of physical force or harm.

Which means those number are inflated due to the ambiguous definition of what sexually assaulted means

Worth noting that the survey was...

In the University of Kentucky survey, released on Monday, the school asked students about unwanted experiences, using federally defined guidelines to include voluntary or involuntary incapacitation due to drugs or alcohol [..]

(emphasis mine). So the survey included anyone who had sex when they were drunk and later regretted it.

Speaking from personal experience and testimonies of friends, some degree of unwanted sexual advances happen to pretty much everyone in college. For example, in freshman year in the dorms, a girl who I made it explicitly clear to I wasn't attracted to snuck into my bad after returning from a party and started kissing my neck when I was half-asleep. We were both very drunk. Was this "sexual assault"? Absolutely. Was it awkward as fuck? Yes. Would I want to press charges for it? No. Did it traumatize me for life? I sure as hell hope not.

I think this survey says as much about the mindset and definition of what constitutes "sexual assault" as what actually happens. I highly doubt that 5% of U Kentucky students were raped at knifepoint or similar, but I don't doubt several times that many had experiences that would fall under the strict definition of "sexual assault" if it includes voluntary intoxication and anything that makes them feel awkward.

That being said, I never attended U Kentucky. Maybe it's just a big forced orgy.
